destination.title: CMB statistics, curvature and cosmological prehistory
destination.question: How can CMB statistics, large-angle signatures and spatial curvature constrain inflationary microphysics, initial states, tunneling or bounce histories and quantum-state measures?
destination.summary: Preserves different observable targets and the conditional histories needed to interpret them.

assumptions: Falsification claims apply to specified histories.
Conditioning on structure formation or a quantum-state measure is an additional choice.
conventions: Non-Gaussianity, power-spectrum structure and curvature are distinct observables.
excludes: Unconditional tests of all eternal-inflation or landscape scenarios

sources.title: Non-Gaussianity from Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Numerical integration evolves the background and up to three mode functions for arbitrary momentum triangles. Early subhorizon integrals use partial integration and approximate Bunch–Davies modes; subsequent evolution uses full numerical modes, typically beginning 4–6 e-folds inside the horizon.

sources.title: Open inflation in the landscape

evidence.text: Project tensors with the Sachs-Wolfe line-of-sight formula and matter-era transfer functions; separate wall and residual continuum contributions and expand in 1−Ω0. The late-time calculation neglects dark energy.

sources.title: Spatial Curvature Falsifies Eternal Inflation

evidence.text: The authors calculate linear spatial Ricci curvature R(3)=4∇²ΦN/a², average it over the last-scattering volume using Gauss's law, and evaluate its ensemble variance through Fourier and spherical-harmonic/Bessel decompositions.

sources.title: Loop quantum cosmology, non-Gaussianity, and CMB power asymmetry

evidence.text: Evaluate the imported leading slow-roll bispectrum formula for the excited state and compute the perturbation energy-density difference from Bunch–Davies. The bispectrum state functions use F(k)=|βk|²+αk*βk; energy-density differences are finite for states of at least fourth adiabatic order.

sources.title: Semiclassical predictions regarding a preinflationary era and its effects on the power spectrum

evidence.text: Volterra iteration analyzes an initially conformal-like vacuum. For spectra, WKB data at a matching time define exact zeroth-, second-, or fourth-order adiabatic states; numerical evolution determines their late-time coefficients in an asymptotic Bunch–Davies basis.

sources.title: Non-Gaussianity from Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: ADM perturbation theory in the gauge with no inflaton fluctuations; quantization of ζ in the Bunch–Davies vacuum; cubic interaction Hamiltonian and in-in integration, including the field redefinition accounting for neglected boundary terms.

sources.title: Inflation and the theory of cosmological perturbations

evidence.text: How can inflation address the horizon, flatness and entropy problems while generating quantum perturbations that seed cosmic structure, CMB anisotropies and gravitational waves?

sources.title: Sharp Predictions from Eternal Inflation Patches in D-brane Inflation

evidence.text: Can a quantum-state measure turn broad distributions of CMB observables in warped D3-brane inflation into sharp predictions, and do slow-roll eternal-inflation patches exist once flux-induced potential terms and all six brane coordinates are included?

sources.title: Observational consequences of a landscape

evidence.text: Could a landscape tunneling origin leave observable negative spatial curvature or large-scale CMB signatures, and does conditioning on structure formation make sufficiently long inflation statistically plausible?

sources.title: General double monodromy inflation

evidence.text: Can interrupted monodromy inflation remain compatible with the paper-era CMB bounds when strong-coupling kinetic corrections are included, and what correlated non-Gaussianity and shorter-wavelength gravitational-wave signatures result?

sources.title: Quantum Compositeness of Gravity: Black Holes, AdS and Inflation

evidence.text: Depletion is estimated through two-to-two scattering, with gravitational coupling and occupation-number combinatorics. During inflation, graviton–inflaton scattering has rate Γ_gφ = H α² N Nφ, enhanced relative to graviton–graviton scattering.

sources.title: String-Inspired Running Vacuum—The “Vacuumon”—And the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Integrate the kinetic identity along H(a), then eliminate a from U(a). The output preserves the input equation-of-state dependence and matches background total stress-energy.

sources.title: Testing quantum gravity with primordial gravitational waves

evidence.text: Calculate the one-loop graviton propagator using spin projectors, approximate logarithmic factors by small anomalous powers, and Fourier transform through Euclidean momentum integrals to equal-time spatial correlators and power spectra.

sources.title: Axions, Black Holes and the Detection of Gravitons: from Astrophysics to Cosmology

evidence.text: For cosmology, estimate the gCS condensate using quadratic quantum tensor perturbations and use a dynamical-system treatment of the axion and background. Real and imaginary condensate components are assigned inflationary and metastability roles respectively.

sources.title: Quantum Compositeness of Gravity: Black Holes, AdS and Inflation

evidence.text: AdS applications use homogeneous constituent counting, mean-field criticality, and escape-energy estimates. Large-black-hole properties are inferred from blueshifting soft mass-sourced gravitons through scattering with harder AdS constituents.

sources.title: Quantum Compositeness of Gravity: Black Holes, AdS and Inflation

evidence.text: The metric dictionary uses weak-field Einstein expansions and transition matrix elements between states of longitudinal gravitons. Single-graviton absorption/emission supplies the leading metric coupling; virtual exchange supplies the first nonlinear correction.

sources.title: Inflation from Anomalies

evidence.text: Can chiral gravitational waves generate a gravitational Chern–Simons condensate that drives finite-duration inflation with a gravitational axion? The review examines possible wave sources, quantum-ordering-dependent vacuum instability and periodic potential modulations needed for slow-roll phenomenology.

sources.title: Hypermagnetic Fields and Baryon Asymmetry from Pseudoscalar Inflation

evidence.text: Ensemble-average the anomaly equations to obtain five coupled Boltzmann equations with helicity sourcing and sphaleron conversion. Numerically evolve in x = Dmp/T from reheating to about 10 TeV, using Γw ≈ 25αw⁵T and Γs ≈ 100αs⁵T.

sources.title: Completely dark matter from rapid-turn multifield inflation

evidence.text: Initialize each Fourier mode in the early adiabatic vacuum, integrate through background nonadiabaticity, and extract a settled occupation in the late adiabatic regime.

sources.title: Brane-vector dark matter and its connection to inflation and primordial gravitational waves

evidence.text: The relic calculation uses a longitudinal-vector mode equation, horizon-exit initial conditions and an energy-density integral. The approximate numerical integral value 1.2 is attributed to earlier work; the authors combine this production prescription with brane expansion and a brane-world tensor amplitude.

sources.title: Hypermagnetic Fields and Baryon Asymmetry from Pseudoscalar Inflation

evidence.text: Apply finite-conductivity magnetohydrodynamics, neglecting ∂tE, to obtain E·B = B·(∇×B)/σ. With the assumed field evolution, derive ḣ = −2I exp(2πξ)(Hinf/a)⁵/(σξ⁶), where I = 6.8×10⁻⁴ and ainf = 1.

sources.title: Hypermagnetic Fields and Baryon Asymmetry from Pseudoscalar Inflation

evidence.text: Quantize the transverse gauge field in circular polarizations and solve A±″ + (k² ± αkΦ′/f)A± = 0. Use the amplified mode approximation and a cutoff kc ≈ 2ξaHinf to estimate gauge-field energy and current helicity, retaining the amplified polarization.

sources.title: Completely dark matter from rapid-turn multifield inflation

evidence.text: Convert produced comoving number into today's nonrelativistic density through pre-reheating expansion, radiation matching and post-reheating entropy conservation.

sources.title: Inflection-point inflation and dark matter redux

evidence.text: Can two phenomenological small-field, near-inflection-point inflation potentials satisfy the paper's CMB constraints and produce all cold dark matter through perturbative inflaton decay, while respecting radiative stability, reheating, BBN and Lyman-α restrictions?

sources.title: Implications of quantum gravity for dark matter in the brane-world scenario

evidence.text: Do quantum-gravity consistency conjectures exclude branon dark matter while favoring massive KK gauge boson dark matter, and can inflationary production make the latter observable through CMB and primordial gravitational waves?

sources.title: Dark energy, D-branes and pulsar timing arrays

evidence.text: A broken-power-law template fitted to the numerical peak is tested against NANOGrav 15-year data with PTArcade. The analysis fixes σ = 6, ε = 0.25 and μ = −2, varies log10(Ab/s) and log10(fb/Hz), assumes Hellings–Downs correlations, and uses uniform priors [2,8] and [−10,−6], respectively.

sources.title: Dark energy, D-branes and pulsar timing arrays

evidence.text: The authors numerically evolve scalar and FLRW background equations, initially neglecting the potential. Appendix A obtains the initial Hubble rate by solving a quartic equation for the DBI Lorentz factor and selecting a real root of order unity.

evidence.text: When can shift-symmetric SUGRA chaotic inflation coexist with KKLT-like modulus stabilization once the modulus remains dynamical during inflation, and can the surviving model have observable departures from quadratic inflation?

sources.title: Volume Modulus Inflation and the Gravitino Mass Problem

evidence.text: Can high-scale inflation coexist with a present TeV-scale gravitino in large-volume compactifications, while avoiding destabilization and post-inflationary overshooting of the compactification minimum?

sources.title: Inflation, moduli (de)stabilization and supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can a superpotential that is relatively large during inflation but small in the final vacuum stabilize moduli while allowing Hinf much larger than the final gravitino mass? What happens to stabilization during the termination of hybrid inflation?

sources.title: Combining High-scale Inflation with Low-energy SUSY

evidence.text: Can high-scale inflation coexist with low-energy supersymmetry when modulus stabilization would ordinarily relate the inflationary Hubble scale to today's gravitino mass? The proposed resolution separates stabilization during inflation from stabilization afterward.

sources.title: Moduli Backreaction on Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Can KKLT volume stabilization coexist with cosmological α-attractor inflation without destructive backreaction, and what does their coupling imply for inflationary endpoints and the relation between H and the vacuum gravitino mass?

sources.title: Backreaction in Axion Monodromy, 4-forms and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can the D7-position inflaton be made light independently of the saxions controlling its metric? The proposed superpotential separates its lifting coefficient mu from closed-sector stabilization data in W_0.

sources.title: Large Field Ranges from Aligned and Misaligned Winding

evidence.text: Can the large-field-range effective theory also support the inflationary mass scale while keeping the volume modulus stabilized? A further question is whether an uplift to a suitable positive potential preserves the delicate stabilization.

sources.title: Inflation near a metastable de Sitter vacuum from moduli stabilisation

evidence.text: Can the minimal ingredients producing a perturbatively stabilised metastable de Sitter vacuum also support realistic volume-modulus inflation? How stable is that vacuum, and what additional physics could end inflation?

sources.title: SUGRA chaotic inflation and moduli stabilisation

evidence.text: The authors analyze the SUGRA scalar potential and the covariant mass matrix on curved field space. Numerical integration follows the coupled fields and compares slow-roll parameters projected along the trajectory with the usual potential-based quantities.

sources.title: Volume Modulus Inflation and the Gravitino Mass Problem

evidence.text: Expand at large volume, discard C,D and higher inverse-volume corrections, and integrate out the heavy τs mode through its approximate instantaneous minimum. Separately construct a leading-order two-field radiation tracker and check consistency with the single-field energy fractions.

sources.title: Inflation, moduli (de)stabilization and supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Use the deformed ISS one-loop effective potential obtained by integrating out χ,χ̄, estimate slow-roll parameters and e-foldings, and track the relative ordering of the matter-waterfall and modulus-instability points. Scalar-potential slices illustrate the proposed histories.

sources.title: Combining High-scale Inflation with Low-energy SUSY

evidence.text: The inflationary prefactor e^K K^{X X̄} is engineered to have a minimum in the modulus direction. The authors then analyze post-inflationary scalar stability and the risk of overshooting between the two stabilization minima.

sources.title: Moduli Backreaction on Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Uses boundary expansions, canonical field redefinition, and leading slow-roll expressions to extract predictions. Selected scalar-field simulations illustrate damping of modulus displacement and waterfall evolution; they supply examples rather than an initial-condition probability measure.

sources.title: Backreaction in Axion Monodromy, 4-forms and the Swampland

evidence.text: Remove the lifting source, verify that the other fields remain stabilized, then restore it as a deformation. This tests whether the inflaton mass can be reduced independently of the heavy-field metric scale and compactification control.

sources.title: Hybrid inflation in high-scale supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can supergravity hybrid inflation remain viable with high-scale supersymmetry by cancelling or suppressing the gravitino-dependent inflaton tadpole, while also stabilizing the moduli?

sources.title: Volume modulus inflection point inflation and the gravitino mass problem

evidence.text: Can volume-modulus inflection-point inflation support a gravitino much lighter than the inflationary Hubble scale with simpler superpotentials, and what parameter and initial-condition tuning remains?

sources.title: Deriving the Inflaton in Compactified M-theory with a De Sitter Vacuum

evidence.text: Can flux-free compactified M-theory identify a modulus inflaton, admit de Sitter vacua and keep the remaining moduli stable during inflation at a Hubble scale much larger than the vacuum gravitino mass?

sources.title: Chaotic inflation and supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can supergravity chaotic inflation with functional freedom in the inflaton potential accommodate low-scale supersymmetry breaking, visible matter and reheating while avoiding cosmological problems from light moduli and gravitinos?

sources.title: Challenges for D-brane large-field inflation with stabilizer fields

evidence.text: Can D-brane-generated bilinear superpotentials realize large-field chaotic inflation with a stabilizer after heavy-modulus backreaction, while maintaining stability and separation from moduli and Kaluza–Klein scales?

sources.title: Shift symmetry and inflation in supergravity

evidence.text: Can mildly broken inflaton shift symmetry and modulus stabilization be combined in N=1 supergravity to obtain a sufficiently flat F-term inflationary potential, and how does the resulting two-field evolution differ from chaotic and hybrid inflation?

sources.title: Microscopic Origin of Volume Modulus Inflation

evidence.text: Can identifiable string corrections generate volume-modulus inflection-point inflation and a later large-volume minimum, allowing the gravitino mass to decrease after inflation? How do flux-superpotential tuning and multifield initial conditions constrain this mechanism?

sources.title: Natural Inflation and Low Energy Supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can high-scale natural inflation coexist with low-scale or unbroken supersymmetry while addressing both effective trans-Planckian axion motion and stabilization of the saxionic partners in a string-inspired description?

sources.title: Unified model of D-term inflation

evidence.text: Can D-term hybrid inflation be embedded in supergravity while explaining the FI scale, stabilizing charged scalars and the FI modulus, controlling the η problem, fitting the scalar tilt and avoiding dangerous waterfall cosmic strings?

sources.title: D term inflation

evidence.text: Can D-term-dominated inflation avoid the generic supergravity inflaton mass of order H, and how does this change the inflationary curvature of moduli and other flat directions?

sources.title: Minimal Starobinsky supergravity coupled to a dilaton-axion superfield

evidence.text: Can minimal Starobinsky supergravity retain viable inflation after coupling its massive vector multiplet to a no-scale dilaton-axion multiplet, while stabilizing both added scalars above the inflationary Hubble scale?

The complete source question is organizationally placed within this admitted scope, retaining source-specific systems, regimes and reading limits. This does not assert question equivalence or method applicability.

destinations.title: When can shift-symmetric SUGRA chaotic inflation coexist with KKLT-like modulus stabilization once the modulus remains dynamical during inflation, and can the surviving model have observable departures from quadratic inflation?

Can high-scale inflation coexist with a present TeV-scale gravitino in large-volume compactifications, while avoiding destabilization and post-inflationary overshooting of the compactification minimum?

Can a superpotential that is relatively large during inflation but small in the final vacuum stabilize moduli while allowing Hinf much larger than the final gravitino mass? What happens to stabilization during the termination of hybrid inflation?

Can high-scale inflation coexist with low-energy supersymmetry when modulus stabilization would ordinarily relate the inflationary Hubble scale to today's gravitino mass? The proposed resolution separates stabilization during inflation from stabilization afterward.

Can KKLT volume stabilization coexist with cosmological α-attractor inflation without destructive backreaction, and what does their coupling imply for inflationary endpoints and the relation between H and the vacuum gravitino mass?

Can the D7-position inflaton be made light independently of the saxions controlling its metric? The proposed superpotential separates its lifting coefficient mu from closed-sector stabilization data in W_0.

Can the large-field-range effective theory also support the inflationary mass scale while keeping the volume modulus stabilized? A further question is whether an uplift to a suitable positive potential preserves the delicate stabilization.

Can the minimal ingredients producing a perturbatively stabilised metastable de Sitter vacuum also support realistic volume-modulus inflation? How stable is that vacuum, and what additional physics could end inflation?
